outputs.exact_statement: There is a nonnegative density $F_0$ on $\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3$, with bounded velocity support and $$\int_{\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3} F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\,\mathrm dx\,\mathrm dv<\infty,$$ for which the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation has two distinct global admissible solutions, in the sense of Definition 2, with initial datum $F_0$. On some common initial interval both solutions are strongly continuous in $L^1$, and their collision gains and losses are integrable in space-time-velocity.

For $0\le t\le\overline T$, the sets $\mathcal O_i(t)$ are pairwise disjoint. Moreover, $$\widehat E_j^\sigma\subset
 \{s_j<|y|<e^\eta s_j\}\subset B(0,s_0).$$ At each point of the periodic lift there is therefore at most one label whose enlargement contains that point.

The datum [eq:datum] satisfies $$\int_\Omega F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\,\,\mathrm dx\,\,\mathrm dv<\infty .$$ Its truncations $F_0^{(N)}$, retaining $j\le N$, converge to $F_0$ in mass, energy, and relative entropy. In addition, if $\chi\ge0$ is a fixed bounded smooth compactly supported function of $(x,v)$, periodized after replacing $x$ by $x/s_N$, and $0\le\lambda_N\le L_0<\infty$, then $$F_0^{(N)}+\lambda_Ns_N\chi(x/s_N,v)$$ has the same limiting mass, energy, and relative entropy as $F_0$. For the last assertion $s_0$ may be decreased so that distinct periodic copies of the spatial support of the seed are disjoint.

The constant $C_m$ can be chosen so that $f_i\le m_i$ on $[0,\overline T]$, uniformly in the label. Moreover, almost everywhere along every free characteristic, $$D_tm_i\ge
 \left(1+\tfrac78 |w_i|^2/d_{s_j}^2\right)m_i .
 \label{jet:barrier-derivative}$$ There is a constant $C_\nu$, independent of the label, such that $$P(m_i,m_i)=m_i\nu_{m_i},\qquad
 \nu_{m_i}(v)\le C_\nu\frac K{s_j}(d_{s_j}+|w_i|).
 \label{jet:barrier-collision}$$ Every free core remains in its own spatial enlargement: $$f_i(t,x,v)>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\in\mathcal O_i(t).$$

There is a constant $L$, depending on the fixed parameters, such that after imposing the additional condition $$Ld_0\overline s^9\le1, \label{jet:thermal-comparison}$$ the following statements hold at every time of existence of the finite approximation in $0\le t\le\overline T$.* 1. *For every retained label $i=(j,\sigma,n)$, $$0\le c_i\le f_i+\varepsilon_j m_i,\qquad \varepsilon_j=Ld_{s_j}/s_j . \label{jet:cold-remainder}$$* 2. *At each spatial point call the unique label with $x\in\mathcal O_i(t)$, if one exists and is retained, the main label. Let $c_{\mathrm{main}}$ be that color, or zero, and set $e=c-c_{\mathrm{main}}$. For every $A\ge0$, $$0\le e(t,x,v)\le C_A t^A e^{-4|v|^2}. \label{jet:escaped}$$ The upper bound remains valid after restricting the escaped sum to any subset of its labels.* 3. *If the main label has scale $s$, its velocity measure is bounded by a fixed multiple of $(t+s)^{-1}$ times a sum of admissible probability sheets from Lemma 6. Its free-core contribution has the exact parameterization [eq:core-jacobian] below. The remainder has the smaller velocity-mass coefficient $Cd_s/s^2$. In particular, for every fixed $k\ge0$, $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\langle v\rangle^k c_{\mathrm{main}}\,\,\mathrm dv \le\frac{C_k}{t+s},\qquad \int_{|v|>R}\langle v\rangle^k c_{\mathrm{main}}\,\,\mathrm dv \le\frac{C_k e^{-c_kR^2}}{t+s}\quad(R\ge3). \label{jet:moment-envelope}$$* 4. *For the mixed-cold source in the hot equation, $$\sum_{\substack{i,j\in\mathcal I_N\\i\ne j}} P^b(c_i,c_j)(t,x,v) \le C_A t^{A-1}H(v)\qquad (t>0) \label{jet:mixed-source}$$ for every $A\ge0$, with constants uniform in $N$ and $b$.

Fix $T\in(0,T_0]$. Either the zero-seed approximations of Proposition 16, or any sequence of its cap shots on $[0,T]$, has a subsequence whose total densities $F_N=c_N+h_N$ converge weakly in $L^1([0,T]\times\Omega)$ to a nonnegative density $F$. The subsequence can be chosen so that $F_N(t)\rightharpoonup F(t)$ in $L^1(\Omega)$ at every $t\in[0,T]$, with uniformly small polynomially weighted velocity tails. The limit has the common initial datum [eq:datum], and $$Q^\pm(F,F)\in L^1([0,T]\times\Omega),\qquad F\in C([0,T];L^1(\Omega)).$$ It satisfies every condition of Definition 2 on this interval, including the inequalities at every time. Each such limit has an admissible global continuation. The dormant upper bound, consisting of the cold majorants of Proposition 14 and $t^2H$, passes to a zero-seed limit.

Suppose that $f_n$ and $g_n$ are locally uniformly integrable in $L^1$ on an open time-space-velocity region, and $(\partial_t+v\cdot\nabla_x)f_n=g_n$ there in distributions. The assertion applies both on a spatial torus and locally in $\mathbb R^3$.

*Consequently any sequence along which the five-fold integral has a positive lower bound has, after periodic translations and subselection, convergent endpoint positions and velocities.
